external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network that communicates with the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application receives browser traffic and places jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker process that picks jobs up from the message queue and does the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue onto which the web application puts jobs and from which the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: A database read and written by the background worker; it also stores the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: Configuration read by the web application, including the web application's queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: Configuration read by the worker, including the worker's database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: browser requests
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker process picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: database access
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: read web application config
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read worker config
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network, where the user's browser sits.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the message queue, background worker process, and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because the user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is in the web tier because it is the configuration store for the web application.
assumptions.basis: The source names the web application as running in the web tier but does not explicitly locate its config store; the store is assigned to the associated process tier.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is in the backend tier because it is the configuration store for the background worker process.
assumptions.basis: The source names the background worker process as being in the backend tier but does not explicitly locate its config store; the store is assigned to the associated process tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the worker's database credentials.
